name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,675

clue.text: Scrabble champion's first rule

indicators.note: first points at the opening letter of the word it is attached to, nothing more

blocks.note: the opening letter of champion
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: A tip from the Scrabble world champion about the board game.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrabble looks like the board game, capitalised to fool you; it is the verb meaning to scratch or grab at something.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrabble is to scratch frantically with hands or nails, which is exactly what clawing at something means.

clue.text: Slow boat contrary to expectation returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: but introduces something contrary to what was expected

explanation.surface: A sluggish vessel came back later than anyone expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase in the middle is just a roundabout way of describing the little conjunction 'but'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tub is an informal, slightly mocking word for a clumsy, broad, slow-moving boat.

clue.text: Tense Sun writer Kingsley making waves

blocks.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
taken as written; the italics make it look like the newspaper
Kingsley Amis, the English novelist of Lucky Jim

explanation.surface: A nervous writer for The Sun newspaper, named Kingsley, is causing a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics dress Sun up as the tabloid; it simply supplies its own three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are enormous sea waves set off by undersea earthquakes, so the plural noun matches waves.

clue.text: Feel very hot water up north?

blocks.note: first meaning: to be painfully hot, as skin in the sun
second meaning: in Scotland and northern England, a small stream

explanation.walkthrough: A burn is the Scottish and northern English word for a stream, which is why the water is placed up north.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to be fiercely hot; as a noun in Scots dialect it names a brook or small river.

clue.text: Desire a wife in Scottish town

blocks.note: to desire is to wish
taken as written
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a bride from a particular town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Wishaw is a town in North Lanarkshire, south-east of Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishaw is a real place name, a town in central Scotland, so it is an example of a Scottish town.

clue.text: Fan calm under pressure

blocks.note: first meaning: to blow air on something to lower its temperature
second meaning: unflustered, keeping one's head

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a supporter who keeps calm, but fan here is the verb about moving air.
explanation.definitionFit: To fan something lowers its temperature, and a person who stays composed in a crisis is described as unflappable in the same word.

clue.text: Judge gives verdict: not right for Verne?

definitions.note: the forename that goes before Verne

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation for right is struck out

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
a judge who gives a verdict rules on the case
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A judge delivers a verdict that goes against a man called Verne.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in: the forename that goes before Verne, author of Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. The question mark flags that it is an example, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules is the first name of the French science-fiction novelist Verne, so it is what you write before his surname.

clue.text: Juan's foul: Ray out for month

indicators.note: something fouled up is messed about and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
out can mean wrong or awry, so these letters are put out of order too

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football report: Juan committed a foul, and Ray is now injured and out for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a sports injury bulletin; both footballers' names are the raw letters, each with its own mixing word.
explanation.definitionFit: January is the first of the twelve calendar months, so it is a straightforward example of a month.

clue.text: Fabulous sight, drunken nuncio runs inside

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about out of line, so these letters lurch into a new order
inside says one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written: a nuncio is a papal ambassador
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: The scandalous spectacle of the Pope's ambassador, drunk, running inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous here means belonging to fable, not wonderful; R slips in near the end of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicorn is a creature of myth and fable, so seeing one would be a sight from legend.

clue.text: Canny ferrymen guarding Welsh river

indicators.note: to guard something is to hold it protected inside, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Shrewd boatmen keep watch over a river in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nyfer, also called the Nevern, is a short river in Pembrokeshire, south-west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyfer is the Welsh name of the river Nevern, which flows to the sea at Newport in Pembrokeshire.

clue.text: Understand studious person knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back pushes something backwards, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: a wonk is a swot, someone who studies hard

explanation.surface: Sympathy for a bookish person who has been rebuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: Wonk is slang, chiefly American, for an overly studious person or a policy expert.
explanation.definitionFit: To understand a fact or subject is to know it, to have it grasped in the mind.

clue.text: Excerpt from section in the Choral Symphony

indicators.note: an excerpt is a passage lifted out of a larger text, so the letters are cut from the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A passage taken from one movement of Beethoven's great choral work.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Symphony No. 9, which ends with the Ode to Joy for chorus, is nicknamed the Choral Symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's last symphony is known both by its number and by its nickname, because its finale brings in singers.

clue.text: Long sentence in biography

blocks.note: first meaning: a prison term for the rest of one's days
second meaning: a written account of someone's history

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rambling sentence in a book; the first meaning is a prison term instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge can hand down a whole-of-days prison term, and biographers' books are often titled 'The ... of' a famous person.

clue.text: Bye! Supporter leaving palace in London area

indicators.note: leaving means going away from, so that piece departs and is removed

blocks.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a bye
the Alhambra is the Moorish palace in Granada
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A fan says goodbye and walks out of a palace somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Balham is a district of south London. The palace is the Moorish one in Granada, and the supporter is an undergarment, not a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Balham is a residential neighbourhood in the borough of Wandsworth, south of the Thames, so it names a part of the capital.

clue.text: Practical characters at Hungary's borders?

indicators.note: borders are the edges of something, so only the outside letters are wanted

blocks.note: the opening letter
the two edge letters are read as a pair, one and the other
the closing letter

explanation.surface: A question about which practical letters stand at the frontiers of Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the characters at the borders of the country aloud as a phrase, 'H and Y', and the phrase itself is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handy is useful and convenient in practice, so the adjective means practical.

clue.text: Tight when crossing river in festive days?

indicators.note: crossing means spanning over something, so one piece stretches across and around the other

blocks.note: near is an old word for stingy or mean with money
the Wye is the river along the England and Wales border

explanation.surface: Someone stingy, out crossing a river over the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: Tight here means miserly, and near is its old-fashioned British equivalent; the Wye sits in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Year holiday, from Hogmanay to New Year's Day, is a period of celebration and parties.

clue.text: Tricky Dick swaps vote for new material

indicators.note: to swap is to exchange one thing for another, so one letter is replaced

blocks.note: Tricky Dick was the nickname of US president Richard Nixon
a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Nixon changes his vote in favour of fresh material.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the X in NIXON with N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer fabric of silk or nylon used for dresses and curtains, so it is a type of cloth.

clue.text: Partner no longer works to raise bonus

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising something lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
works of art

explanation.surface: A former spouse goes out to earn some extra cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Works as in works of art; in a down entry 'raise' sends the letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is something additional on top of the usual, and extra means exactly an added payment or item.

clue.text: Private saving beneficiary managed without yen

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Someone who benefits from private savings managed without any Japanese money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without yen' reads as 'lacking yen', but without means outside here. The definition rearranges the film title Saving Private Ryan.
explanation.definitionFit: In the 1998 Spielberg war film, a squad is sent to rescue Private James Ryan, so he is the one whom the saving benefits.

clue.text: Using sound, very delicate note dropped

indicators.note: something dropped is let go and left out, so that letter is lost

blocks.note: so means very, as in so kind
nice in its older sense of fine, subtle, delicate
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A musician played a very soft note that dropped out of hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice once meant fine or delicate, as in a nice distinction; the final E falls off.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to or operating by sound waves, as in sonic boom or sonic weapon.

clue.text: Two going round on their Bromptons?

definitions.text: Two going round on their Bromptons?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pair of people doing the rounds together
setter's reading: riders turning wheels on folding bikes

explanation.walkthrough: A Brompton is a popular British folding bicycle; 'two going round' is also the pair of wheels that spin.
explanation.definitionFit: People who ride bicycles, such as the folding Brompton made in London, are the riders the clue pictures.

clue.text: Audibly changed direction in diplomacy

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the words are judged by how they sound

blocks.note: a sailing boat tacks when it turns into the wind onto a new course

explanation.surface: A diplomat who makes a noisy U-turn in negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacking is the sailing manoeuvre of turning the bow through the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomacy in everyday dealings is the sensitive handling of people, which is what we call skill in avoiding offence.

clue.text: Pet for daughter in London district?

blocks.note: a cat is a common pet
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Looking for a pet for a daughter somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Catford is a district of south-east London, in the borough of Lewisham.
explanation.definitionFit: Catford is a town-centre neighbourhood within Greater London, so it is an example of a district of the city.

clue.text: Rhys Jones for audience on as monster

indicators.note: an audience listens, so this is what is heard rather than what is written

blocks.note: Griff Rhys Jones is a Welsh comedian and television presenter
taken as written

explanation.surface: The comedian Rhys Jones appears on stage dressed as a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Griff Rhys Jones, of Alas Smith and Jones, supplies the sound of the first syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: A gryphon, or griffin, is a mythical beast with an eagle's head and wings and a lion's body.

clue.text: Designer good one around posh clubs twice

indicators.note: around says one piece encircles the other

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
I is the Roman numeral for one
U means upper class, as in U and non-U
C is the card abbreviation for clubs, used two times

explanation.surface: A fashion designer who is a good sort, going around exclusive clubs night after night.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the first two letters side by side, then open them up to take the other three.
explanation.definitionFit: Gucci is the Italian fashion house, a classic name in luxury designer goods.

clue.text: Samuel's mum unaffected by revolution

indicators.note: a word that is unchanged when turned round reads the same backwards and forwards

blocks.note: in the Bible, the mother of the prophet Samuel

explanation.surface: The prophet's mother stays calm through an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition gives the name; the rest only confirms that the name reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: In the First Book of Samuel, Hannah prays for a child and gives birth to the prophet Samuel.

clue.text: Decent being close to target in hunt

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is taken
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: the closing letter
a hunt is a chase

explanation.surface: A respectable hunter who has nearly reached the quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to target' suggests being near the aim; it means the last letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and modest in behaviour, which is a sense of decent as morally proper.

clue.text: Endless fright and surgery reminder?

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter is cut away

blocks.note: a fright is a scare

explanation.surface: The never-ending fear of an operation and the mark it leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation leaves a healed mark on the skin, a lasting physical souvenir of the incision.

clue.text: Hitch the Master of Suspense directed it!

definitions.text: the Master of Suspense directed it

blocks.note: first meaning: to tie up or tether, as you would a horse

blocks.clueFragment: the Master of Suspense directed it
blocks.note: second meaning: a 1948 thriller by Alfred Hitchcock, known as the Master of Suspense

explanation.walkthrough: Hitch looks like Hitchcock's nickname, priming you to read the whole clue as one film reference; it is the verb meaning to tie. The film was shot to look like one continuous take.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch a horse is to tether it with cord, and Hitchcock's 1948 single-take thriller starring James Stewart has the same one-word title.

clue.text: Old article about motorway woman

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the letters before it run backwards

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
an is the indefinite article
the M1 motorway, with the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece from the past about a woman on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London; crosswords write it as MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female first name, so it stands for a woman as crossword definitions often do.

clue.text: Love at hotel to make promise

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
taken as written
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two lovers meet at a hotel to exchange vows.
explanation.walkthrough: The romantic surface hides tennis scoring, where love means nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn vow or sworn pledge, so the noun matches promise.

clue.text: Set piece player involved in scrum

blocks.note: first meaning: an object used on a theatre or film set
second meaning: a rugby forward in the front row

explanation.walkthrough: Set piece sounds like a rugby term, which fits the scrum, but it means an item on a stage set.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage property is an object actors handle, and in rugby the front-row forwards either side of the hooker share the same name.

clue.text: Old man seen with Irish couple

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Someone's father spotted out with an Irish couple.
explanation.walkthrough: Old man is slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two people or things together, so it is a synonym for a couple.

clue.text: Fix where Blythe admits to spying?

blocks.note: the setter speaking in the first person says I'm
a plant is someone placed undercover to spy

explanation.surface: A setup in which the setter confesses to being a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Blythe is the setter of this puzzle, so Blythe's confession is 'I'm a plant'.
explanation.definitionFit: To implant is to fix something firmly in place, embedding it in tissue or in the mind.

clue.text: Gang in Caribbean island denied new papers

indicators.note: something denied is refused and kept out, so these letters are withheld

blocks.note: Trinidad, the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago
N is the abbreviation for new
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A criminal gang on a Caribbean island refused fresh documents.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N and ID out of the middle of the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a Chinese organised crime syndicate, so it is a kind of criminal gang.

clue.text: Husband given arsenic suffers

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: A poisoned husband falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The poisoning surface hides a chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To have an illness is to suffer from it, as in 'she has flu', so the verb forms match.
